bug_semantics: Sample executor handler SampleXxlJob.httpJobHandler treats the job parameter URL as an open HTTP client: it parses url/method/data from XxlJobHelper.getJobParam() (JSON map at 3.1.x; earlier url:/method:/data: text), then does new URL(url) + HttpURLConnection.openConnection() with no destination allowlist or block of loopback/link-local/RFC1918/metadata. An actor who can hit the executor /run API with a valid XXL-JOB-ACCESS-TOKEN (or who can set job params in admin) can force the executor to fetch arbitrary URLs, which is CWE-918 SSRF. The handler lives in xxl-job-executor-samples, not xxl-job-core; GHSA still maps the Maven package to com.xuxueli:xxl-job-core. CVE.org remains PUBLISHED (not REJECTED). Owner later landed an explicit CVE-2025-7787 URL whitelist rather than withdrawing the issue.
flaw_origin: The SSRF mechanism was first written on 2018-09-16 in a1755156e2da257b0c3708bfbf34d876d91dfb2c as new sample class HttpJobHandler.execute: it took the raw job param as an HTTP URL (Apache HttpGet(param) in spring/springboot samples) with only empty-string validation. Later non-BIC refactors kept that unvalidated request: 573facc05051a30dbe858e643486b9f15bf85211 swapped the client to HttpURLConnection/new URL(param); 9fed7b9c602560723ad07f3feb518308fa282345 moved the method into SampleXxlJob.httpJobHandler (deleted HttpJobHandler.java); 239200e52c5e5b69c559fd6c485a26d5c97b9d6d added url:/method:/data: parsing (the GHSA/issue snippet); 4af184721446e81c417797b7025b93fd35acdc35 switched params to JSON. None of those first-wrote the missing destination check. Parent d6dc40b49e7243fb782009de451db390b67fd67c has Demo/Sharding handlers only, no HttpJobHandler.java.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2025-7787/GHSA-f8vw-8vgh-22r9 describe SSRF in SampleXxlJob.httpJobHandler. CVE.org is PUBLISHED and GHSA is not withdrawn, so this is not FALSE_POSITIVE even though the code is a sample executor and GHSA labels the wrong Maven artifact (xxl-job-core). At affected tag 3.1.1 the handler still opens HttpURLConnection to a job-param URL with no allowlist; issue 3749's POC used the older url:\nmethod: text format, but 3.1.x already accepted JSON {url,method,data} with the same sink. BIC search started from that sink, not from AI-marked commits. git log -L on SampleXxlJob at 3.1.1 bottoms out at the 2019-12-12 method-mode move (9fed7b9c), which deleted HttpJobHandler.java and copied the unvalidated new URL(param) request into SampleXxlJob; a move is not a BIC. Pickaxe -S httpJobHandler / HttpURLConnection / 'url:' then git show of HttpJobHandler.java shows the first write of the unvalidated job-param HTTP request is a1755156e2da257b0c3708bfbf34d876d91dfb2c (2018-09-16), adding HttpJobHandler to four samples. Immediate parent d6dc40b49e7243fb782009de451db390b67fd67c has no HttpJobHandler.java. Intermediate HttpURLConnection and JSON-format commits are refactors of the same missing destination check. The smallest surviving public object that first introduced the flawed mechanism is therefore a1755156; it is a single-parent non-squash commit. AI judgment uses only that commit object: human author/committer xuxueli, no AI trailers, so NOT_AI. Remediation is c741d8361ee91910c4198a70c646e92a70db7c45 (explicit CVE-2025-7787 URL whitelist), first released in tag 3.2.0, after the GHSA affected bound 3.1.1.
